title: Typical Redis applications
context: What are the common uses of Redis in production?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Caching database results with a TTL is the most common use. Other uses: session storage, rate limiting with INCR and EXPIRE, counters and statistics, leaderboards with sorted sets, distributed locks with SET NX PX, pub/sub notifications, and simple queues with lists or streams. Each use depends on the right data type and on handling expiry, eviction and failure of the Redis server.

points.title: Caching with TTL
points.why: Cached values need an expiry so stale data eventually goes away.

points.title: Atomic counters and locks
points.why: INCR and SET NX give atomic operations that rate limiters and locks rely on.
